title: From Mastery Profile to Simulated Response: Stochastic Student Knowledge Graphs (SSKG) for Faithful LLM Student Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2608.21668v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate students at different mastery levels. These simulations can generate synthetic training data and stress-test tutoring systems. However, common prompt-based approaches leave the answer decision to the LLM, which tends to perform according to its built-in capabilities even when instructed to simulate a student with low mastery. As a result, these approaches may have difficulty distinguishing students with low and high levels of mastery. We demonstrate this limitation using 379 College Board-calibrated SAT Algebra items and five archetypal mastery profiles. Three LLMs from three vendors (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, Claude Haiku 4.5, and GPT-5.4-mini) achieve 96.8-100% accuracy across all profiles. translated_title: 从掌握度画像到模拟响应：用于忠实大语言模型学生模拟的随机学生知识图谱（SSKG）
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.21668v1 公告类型：新 摘要：大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于模拟不同掌握水平的学生。这些模拟可以生成合成训练数据，并对辅导系统进行压力测试。然而，常见的基于提示的方法将答题决策交给大语言模型，即使被指示模拟低掌握水平的学生，模型也倾向于根据其内置能力进行表现。因此，这些方法可能难以区分低掌握和高掌握水平的学生。我们使用379道经大学理事会校准的SAT代数题目和五种典型掌握度画像来证明这一局限性。来自三家供应商的三个大语言模型（Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite、Claude Haiku 4.5和GPT-5.4-mini）在所有画像上实现了96.8%至100%的准确率。为解决这一局限性，我们引入了一种基于随机学生知识图谱（SSKG）的方法。从一本开放代数教科书中提取课程知识图谱（CKG），并...
tldr: 本文提出基于随机学生知识图谱（SSKG）的方法，以解决大语言模型在模拟低掌握水平学生时因内置能力导致难以区分掌握程度差异的问题，从而实现更忠实的学生模拟。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a Stochastic Student Knowledge Graph (SSKG)-based method to address the limitation that large language models fail to distinguish mastery levels when simulating low-proficiency students due to their built-in capabilities, enabling more faithful student simulation.
